question:
Case Study: Portfolio Investment and Linear System Consistency

An investor allocates funds to stocks A, B, and C, expecting returns modelled by:

$\begin{cases} x + 2y + 3z = 10000 \\ 2x + 3y + z = 8000 \\ 3x + y + 2z = 12000 \end{cases}$

(a) Express this as a matrix equation and determine if the coefficient matrix is invertible.

(b) Use the matrix method to find if a unique solution for $(x,y,z)$ exists and, if so, compute it.

(c) Critically analyze what the consistency or inconsistency of this investment system implies for portfolio planning.
explanation:
(a)

$\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 10000 \\ 8000 \\ 12000 \end{bmatrix}$

Test invertibility: compute $|A|$.

Expand: $1\left|\begin{matrix}3&1\\1&2\end{matrix}\right|-2\left|\begin{matrix}2&1\\3&2\end{matrix}\right|+3\left|\begin{matrix}2&3\\3&1\end{matrix}\right|$

First term: $1(3\times2-1\times1)=1(6-1)=5$

Second: $-2(2\times2-3\times1)=-2(4-3) = -2$

Third: $+3(2\times1-3\times3)=3(2-9) = 3(-7)=-21$

Sum: $5-2-21 = -18$ (not zero)

So, invertible.

(b)

Use $A^{-1}$ to solve:

$\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = A^{-1}\begin{bmatrix} 10000 \\ 8000 \\ 12000 \end{bmatrix}$

Compute $A^{-1}$ (computationally intensive, can be assigned as steps or use technology).

(c)

If $|A| \neq 0$, the system is consistent and independent; there is a unique way to allocate funds. If $|A|=0$, then the system is either dependent (infinite solutions) or inconsistent (no solution), meaning conflicting or redundant investment expectations.

options.A:
(a) $\begin{bmatrix}1&2&3\\2&3&1\\3&1&2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}10000\\8000\\12000\end{bmatrix}$ and $|A|=0$.
(b) No unique solution exists.
(c) The system is inconsistent.
options.B:
(a) $\begin{bmatrix}1&2&3\\2&3&1\\3&1&2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}10000\\8000\\12000\end{bmatrix}$ and $|A|=-18\ne0$, so the coefficient matrix is invertible.
(b) A unique solution exists: $x=\frac{7000}{3}$, $y=\frac{1000}{3}$, $z=\frac{7000}{3}$.
(c) Since the system is consistent with a unique solution, the portfolio allocation is determined uniquely.
options.C:
(a) The coefficient matrix is singular.
(b) Infinitely many solutions exist.
(c) Portfolio planning has no fixed allocation.
options.D:
(a) Matrix equation is $AX=0$.
(b) $x=10000$, $y=8000$, $z=12000$.
(c) The equations are redundant.
